text: Thanks — I'm on it. I've started an investigation into why `required=True` is ignored for `is_flag=True` boolean options (`--on/--off`). I'll have it reproduced, fixed and tested shortly; ETA ~10 minutes.

Got it — the `pythonw.exe` crash is because click's default stdout/stderr can be `None` when no console is attached, and `echo`/`progressbar`/pager then call `.write` on it. I've started a second investigation to make those paths silently drop output instead of raising. ETA ~12 minutes (the flag bug is still in progress).

Fixed and verified. Cause: in `Option.__init__` (src/click/core.py), when `is_flag=True` and no `default=` was given, click force-set `self.default = False`. That implicit default meant the value was never "missing", so the `required` check in `Parameter.process_value` never fired. The fix only applies that implicit default when the option is not required, so `--on/--off` with `required=True` now keeps `default=None` and errors with `Error: Missing option '--on'` (exit code 2). `--on` -> True, `--off` -> False still work, and the full test suite is unchanged (488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed).

Right — an option with `flag_value` set should behave as a flag, so an envvar that is merely *set* should yield the configured `flag_value` (`upper`), not the raw envvar text. I've started a third investigation into the envvar handling for flag options. ETA ~12 minutes.

Understood — a decorator built once with `cls=` should work on every command it's applied to. I've started a fourth investigation into how the shared parameter object is handled when the same decorator is applied to a second command. ETA ~12 minutes.

Confirmed as a bug — `resolve_path=True` should give the absolute real path (`/tmp/demo/real.txt`), and relative symlink targets are being resolved against the wrong base directory. I've started a fifth investigation into `click.Path` in src/click/types.py. ETA ~12 minutes.

Fixed and verified. Cause: in `Path.convert` (src/click/types.py) the code called `os.readlink()` first and then `os.path.realpath()`. `os.readlink` returns the raw link target (`real.txt`), which is relative to the symlink's own directory, but it was then resolved against the current working directory — hence `/real.txt`. The manual readlink step was only a Windows-<3.8 fallback, so it now uses `pathlib.Path(...).resolve()` (with a bytes branch preserved). `/tmp/demo/link` now yields `/tmp/demo/real.txt`; chains, directory links, `..` targets, absolute links, `path_type=pathlib.Path`/`bytes`, and `resolve_path=False` all behave correctly. Full suite unchanged: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed.

Agreed — with a default map value of `True` the flag takes the `name` value, so `--help` should show `default: name`. I've started a sixth investigation into how `get_help_record` builds the default string (it currently only consults the option's own default, ignoring `ctx.default_map`). ETA ~12 minutes.

Fixed and verified. Cause: with `pythonw.exe` there is no console, so `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` are `None`. Click's cached default text streams (`_make_cached_stream_func` in src/click/_compat.py) happily returned that `None`, and `echo` (src/click/utils.py), `ProgressBar` and the pager (src/click/_termui_impl.py) then called `.write` on it. Now the cached stream helper propagates `None`, `echo` simply drops the output, and `progressbar`/`echo_via_pager` fall back to a throwaway sink. Reproduced all five paths (echo, secho, echo(err=True), echo_via_pager, progressbar) raising AttributeError before, and exiting cleanly with no output after. Normal output/color behavior is unchanged and the full suite still passes (488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed).

Fixed and verified. Cause: in `argument()` (src/click/decorators.py) the inner decorator did `ArgumentClass = attrs.pop("cls", Argument)`, which *removes* `cls` from the dict captured by the decorator closure. So the first command got `MyArgument` and every later application fell back to plain `Argument`. `option()` already copied its attrs first (the earlier Issue-926 fix), so only `argument` was affected. `argument` now copies attrs before popping, so a shared decorator yields the custom class for every command (verified for commands, groups, reuse after invocation, and with `required`/`nargs`/`default`/`metavar`/`help`/`is_flag`/`multiple`/`prompt` combinations). Full suite unchanged: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed.

Fixed and verified. Cause: in `Option.get_help_record` (src/click/core.py), the `--flag/--no-flag` branch built the default string from the raw `self.default` instead of the already-resolved `default_value = self.get_default(ctx, call=False)`, which is what consults `ctx.default_map`. Every other branch used the resolved value, so only boolean flags ignored the default map. That branch now picks `self.opts` vs `self.secondary_opts` from `default_value`, so a default-map value of `True` renders `[default: name]` (and `False` still renders `[default: no-name]`). Verified against default maps for flags, non-flags, `count`, `multiple`, callable defaults, `show_default` as a string/False, and `context_settings`. Full suite unchanged: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed.
